109550d2e94e.title: J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home clinic candidate
109550d2e94e.content: J3, Clinic verification and schedule generation, in Country B. The clinic EHR (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, VHL Receiver side in IHE ITI VHL) holds a copy of the GDHCN trust list, which the trust anchor (Trust Network Anchor; IHE Trust Anchor) distributes and Country B, a Trust Network Participant, [retrieves (smart-trust-phw retrieve-pki-material)](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-phw/artifact/Requirements-retrieve-pki-material.html). Loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the clinic may be offline throughout, so the list it verifies against is the one it last refreshed, about weekly, when the CHW visits the base clinic or district health office. It verifies each foreign DVC in the STT-VER-001 order against XXR's DSC DID document, imports the verified doses with provenance, adds the national schedule code beside each foreign vaccine code (ConceptMap; the nurse decides any product with no mapping) and evaluates the national schedule, which finds the 6-week doses due and books them. Also called: J3 Verify, import and schedule .

9fb07ad45c6c.doc: J1 Issue the newborn's birth-dose DVCs in Country A
9fb07ad45c6c.title: J1 Issue the newborn’s birth-dose DVCs in Country A candidate
9fb07ad45c6c.content: J1, Cross-border birth and initial vaccination. In Country A (XXR, the birth country) the provincial hospital gives a newborn who is not its own country's national the Hep B and BCG birth doses and issues one signed DVC per dose (DVCMinPreQual at subclaim -6) as a paper QR, with no national identity number needed (the WHO guide's QR Code Generation section 12 example is such a pair). The hospital system is the Issuer (SMART Trust) and the HCERT side of the VHL Sharer; the private key stays with the key holder (two-phase signing, STT-ISS-004, STT-COS-006). XXR's DSC, under its CSCA, being on the GDHCN trust list is a PRECONDITION of issuing, declared below, not a step. The caregiver is the Holder (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) and VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL). Also called: J1 Issue the birth-dose DVCs .

015edd0d16e9.doc: J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad
015edd0d16e9.title: J4.1 Read a family member’s records at the point of care abroad candidate
015edd0d16e9.content: J4.1. Abroad, a child of the family needs care. The caregiver, the VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL; Holder in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver), opens her QR on the family phone and tells the passcode. The hospital system, a VHL Receiver (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw), verifies the HCERT against the GDHCN trust list, requests the manifest by ITI-YY5 with an HTTP Message Signature (STT-VHL-005, STT-VHL-006, STT-VHL-008) and decrypts the documents (STT-VHL-007). Country B's portal checks the passcode, returns the manifest and logs every request, granted or refused, as an AuditEvent at home (IHE BALP). If the HCERT does not verify, there is no digital verification: the VHL is not followed and the records are treated like paper. As in J3, loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the hospital verifies against its cached copy of the trust list and needs no connection to do so. It refreshes that cache nightly or hourly, where an offline site such as the J3 clinic refreshes about weekly. Also called: J4.1 Read records at the point of care .

5a1cf29fb68d.doc: J4.0 Issue the family's records to one phone as VHLs
5a1cf29fb68d.title: J4.0 Issue the family’s records to one phone as VHLs candidate
5a1cf29fb68d.content: J4.0, Outbound family travel, "One Family, One Phone". Before travelling, the caregiver who holds the family's one shared phone asks Country B's national portal for each family member's records, choosing for each a passcode the family can say aloud and an expiry (for example 14 days); the portal records that choice as the holder's consent to share (FHIR Consent, IHE Privacy Consent on FHIR). The portal, a VHL Sharer (IHE ITI VHL) and Issuer (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw), issues one passcode-protected Verifiable Health Link per member: the documents (IPS, DVCs) encrypted as JWE (STT-VHL-007) behind an ITI-YY5 manifest, the link in the SMART Health Links payload format at HCERT key 5 (STT-VHL-001, STT-VHL-002), signed with Country B's DSC. The shared phone holds the QRs for the caregiver, the VHL Holder. The records themselves stay hosted in Country B: the QR carries only a pointer and a key. Also called: J4.0 Issue the family’s VHLs .

e9500603bde4.doc: J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant in Country B
e9500603bde4.title: J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant in Country B candidate
e9500603bde4.content: J2, Return home, CHW discovery and referral. Back in Country B (home, XXU), where the family resides, the community health worker finds an infant born abroad who is missing from the household roster on a home visit. Offline, the CHW app adds the infant to the household (a FHIR Group, through a structured data capture form), reads the foreign DVCs without verifying them (read-unverified, STT-VER-011: the triage read stops before the trust lookup and marks every field unverified), saves the doses as reported by the family, not verified (Immunization.primarySource false), and refers the infant to the clinic for verification. Everything is queued on the phone and syncs when it next has a signal. The CHW app is a Receiver (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) that deliberately stops before trust; the caregiver provides the VDHC as Holder (smart-trust-phw requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver). Also called: J2 Discover and refer the infant .

1fa7a722fe9b.title: J
1fa7a722fe9b.content: J1 Issue the newborn's birth-dose DVCs in Country A candidate J1, Cross-border birth and initial vaccination. In Country A (XXR, the birth country) the provincial hospital gives a newborn who is not its own country's national the Hep B and BCG birth doses and issues one signed DVC per dose (DVCMinPreQual at subclaim -6) as a paper QR, with no national identity number needed (the WHO guide's QR Code Generation section 12 example is such a pair). The hospital system is the Issuer (SMART Trust) and the HCERT side of the VHL Sharer; the private key stays with the key holder (two-phase signing, STT-ISS-004, STT-COS-006). XXR's DSC, under its CSCA, being on the GDHCN trust list is a PRECONDITION of issuing, declared below, not a step. The caregiver is the Holder (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) and VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL). Term page · SMART Trust demonstrator architecture · https://worldhealthorganization.github.io/smart-trust-demo/v0/ns/glossary/architecture/journey-j1 · source processes/content/j1-birth-dose-dvc.bpmn#Process_J1BirthDoseDvc . Depicted in ArchiMate smart-trust-demo 0.1.0: J1 Issue the newborn's birth-dose DVCs in Country A (BusinessProcess); views: SMART Trust demo journeys (use cases), J1 on the DPI-H RA . J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant in Country B candidate J2, Return home, CHW discovery and referral. Back in Country B (home, XXU), where the family resides, the community health worker finds an infant born abroad who is missing from the household roster on a home visit. Offline, the CHW app adds the infant to the household (a FHIR Group, through a structured data capture form), reads the foreign DVCs without verifying them (read-unverified, STT-VER-011: the triage read stops before the trust lookup and marks every field unverified), saves the doses as reported by the family, not verified (Immunization.primarySource false), and refers the infant to the clinic for verification. Everything is queued on the phone and syncs when it next has a signal. The CHW app is a Receiver (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) that deliberately stops before trust; the caregiver provides the VDHC as Holder (smart-trust-phw requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver). Term page · SMART Trust demonstrator architecture · https://worldhealthorganization.github.io/smart-trust-demo/v0/ns/glossary/architecture/journey-j2 · source processes/content/j2-chw-discovery-referral.bpmn#Process_J2ChwDiscovery . Depicted in ArchiMate smart-trust-demo 0.1.0: J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant in Country B (BusinessProcess); views: SMART Trust demo journeys (use cases), J2 on the DPI-H RA . J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home clinic candidate J3, Clinic verification and schedule generation, in Country B. The clinic EHR (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, VHL Receiver side in IHE ITI VHL) holds a copy of the GDHCN trust list, which the trust anchor (Trust Network Anchor; IHE Trust Anchor) distributes and Country B, a Trust Network Participant, [retrieves (smart-trust-phw retrieve-pki-material)](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-phw/artifact/Requirements-retrieve-pki-material.html). Loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the clinic may be offline throughout, so the list it verifies against is the one it last refreshed, about weekly, when the CHW visits the base clinic or district health office. It verifies each foreign DVC in the STT-VER-001 order against XXR's DSC DID document, imports the verified doses with provenance, adds the national schedule code beside each foreign vaccine code (ConceptMap; the nurse decides any product with no mapping) and evaluates the national schedule, which finds the 6-week doses due and books them. Term page · SMART Trust demonstrator architecture · https://worldhealthorganization.github.io/smart-trust-demo/v0/ns/glossary/architecture/journey-j3 · source processes/content/j3-clinic-verification-schedule.bpmn#Process_J3ClinicVerification . Depicted in ArchiMate smart-trust-demo 0.1.0: J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home clinic (BusinessProcess); views: SMART Trust demo journeys (use cases), J3 on the DPI-H RA . J4.0 Issue the family's records to one phone as VHLs candidate J4.0, Outbound family travel, "One Family, One Phone". Before travelling, the caregiver who holds the family's one shared phone asks Country B's national portal for each family member's records, choosing for each a passcode the family can say aloud and an expiry (for example 14 days); the portal records that choice as the holder's consent to share (FHIR Consent, IHE Privacy Consent on FHIR). The portal, a VHL Sharer (IHE ITI VHL) and Issuer (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw), issues one passcode-protected Verifiable Health Link per member: the documents (IPS, DVCs) encrypted as JWE (STT-VHL-007) behind an ITI-YY5 manifest, the link in the SMART Health Links payload format at HCERT key 5 (STT-VHL-001, STT-VHL-002), signed with Country B's DSC. The shared phone holds the QRs for the caregiver, the VHL Holder. The records themselves stay hosted in Country B: the QR carries only a pointer and a key. Term page · SMART Trust demonstrator architecture · https://worldhealthorganization.github.io/smart-trust-demo/v0/ns/glossary/architecture/journey-j4-0 · source processes/content/j4-0-family-vhl-issuance.bpmn#Process_J40FamilyVhl . Depicted in ArchiMate smart-trust-demo 0.1.0: J4.0 Issue the family's records to one phone as VHLs (BusinessProcess); views: SMART Trust demo journeys (use cases), J4.0 on the DPI-H RA . J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad candidate J4.1. Abroad, a child of the family needs care. The caregiver, the VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL; Holder in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver), opens her QR on the family phone and tells the passcode. The hospital system, a VHL Receiver (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw), verifies the HCERT against the GDHCN trust list, requests the manifest by ITI-YY5 with an HTTP Message Signature (STT-VHL-005, STT-VHL-006, STT-VHL-008) and decrypts the documents (STT-VHL-007). Country B's portal checks the passcode, returns the manifest and logs every request, granted or refused, as an AuditEvent at home (IHE BALP). If the HCERT does not verify, there is no digital verification: the VHL is not followed and the records are treated like paper. As in J3, loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the hospital verifies against its cached copy of the trust list and needs no connection to do so. It refreshes that cache nightly or hourly, where an offline site such as the J3 clinic refreshes about weekly.
